{{Infobox Election | election_name = United States House of Representatives elections in Arizona, 2018 | country = Arizona | type = legislative | ongoing = no | previous_election = United States House of Representatives elections in Arizona, 2016 | previous_year = 2016 | next_election = United States House of Representatives elections in Arizona, 2020 | next_year = 2020 | seats_for_election = Arizona's nine seats in the [[United States House of Representatives]] | election_date = {{Start date|2018|11|06}} | party1 = Republican Party (United States) | last_election1 = 5 | seats1 = | seat_change1 = | popular_vote1 = | percentage1 = | swing1 = | party2 = Democratic Party (United States) | last_election2 = 4 | seats2 = | seat_change2 = | popular_vote2 = | percentage2 = | swing2 = | map_image = | map_caption = }} {{ElectionsAZ}} The '''2018 United States House of Representatives elections in Arizona''' will be held on November 6, 2018, to elect the nine [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representatives]] from the [[U.S. state|state]] of [[Arizona]], one from each of the state's nine [[Arizona's congressional districts|congressional districts]]. The elections coincide with the [[Arizona gubernatorial election, 2018|2018 Arizona gubernatorial election]], as well as [[United States House of Representatives elections, 2018|other elections]] to the House of Representatives, [[United States Senate elections, 2018|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]] and various [[United States elections, 2018#State elections|state]] and [[United States elections, 2018#Local elections|local elections]]. {{Toclimit|limit=2}} == District 1 == {{see also|Arizona's 1st congressional district}} The 1st district is home to the [[Grand Canyon]] and stretches along the eastern and northeastern portions of the state and includes [[Casa Grande, AZ|Casa Grande]], [[Flagstaff, AZ|Flagstaff]], and [[Marana, AZ|Marana]]. This district has a significant Native-American population, making up 25% of the population in the district. Also this district is home to many Indian reservations such as: the [[Gila River Indian Community]], [[Hopi Reservation]], and the [[Navajo Nation]]. Incumbent Democratic Congressman [[Tom O'Halleran]], won election to his first term in 2016 with 50.90 percent of the vote over Republican sheriff [[Paul Babeu]].{{cite news |url=http://results.arizona.vote/2016/General/n1591/Results-State.html |title=2016 General Election November 8, 2016 Unofficial Results |date=November 8, 2016 |publisher=Arizona Secretary of State |accessdate=November 15, 2016}} This district is one of the most competitive in the state with a [[Cook Partisan Voting Index|PVI]] of R+2. This is one of 36 Democratic-held House districts targeted by the [[National Republican Congressional Committee]] in 2018.{{cite web |url=https://www.nrcc.org/2017/02/08/nrcc-announces-initial-offensive-targets-2018-cycle/ |title=NRCC Announces Initial Offensive Targets For The 2018 Cycle |publisher=NRCC |author= |date=February 8, 2017 |accessdate=April 15, 2018}} === Democratic primary === ;Candidates * [[Tom O'Halleran]],https://apps.arizona.vote/electioninfo/elections/2018-primary-election/federal/1347/3/0 incumbent ;Withdrew *Miguel Olivashttps://www.pinalcentral.com/casa_grande_dispatch/area_news/cd-ld-candidates-withdraw-from-races-after-court-challenges/article_3481a809-03d4-5159-b3e0-a01bd7880506.html ====Primary results==== {{Election box begin no change | title=Democratic primary results}} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change |party = Democratic Party (United States) |candidate = [[Tom O'Halleran]] (incumbent) |votes = 64,114 |percentage = 100.0 }} {{Election box total no change | votes = 64,114 | percentage = 100.0 }} {{Election box end}} === Republican primary === ==== Candidates ==== *Tiffany Shedd,https://apps.arizona.vote/electioninfo/elections/2018-primary-election/federal/1347/3/0 attorney{{cite news |url=http://www.pinalcentral.com/arizona_city_independent/news/shedd-announces-gop-bid-for-congress/article_ed7892ed-d546-5b4a-adc5-54e53cf7e54b.html |title=Shedd announces GOP bid for Congres s|author=Heather Smathers |date= |newspaper=Arizona City Independent |accessdate=April 15, 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://ballotpedia.org/Tiffany_Shedd|title=Tiffany Shedd |publisher=Ballotpedia |accessdate=April 15, 2018}} *Wendy Rogers,https://apps.arizona.vote/electioninfo/elections/2018-primary-election/federal/1347/3/0 retired Air Force pilot and perennial candidate{{cite news |url=http://ktar.com/story/1916491/republican-wendy-rogers-announces-run-for-rep-tom-ohallerans-seat/ |title=Republican Wendy Rogers announces run for Rep.
